gap: No result ChatGPT got states that the Anker SOLIX C1000 Gen 2's 600 W solar rating applies only to panel arrays running at 29–60 V (14.5 A max). From 11 to 28 V the input is capped at 8.2 A, about 230 W. The box contains only an AC charging cable, and Anker's spec sheet lists no car-socket charging input, only a 12 V 120 W car-socket output.
standout_why: I compared against both pages ChatGPT cited, GearJunkie (2026-10-31) and OutdoorGearLab (2026-07-23). Both give the C1000 Gen 2 a flat '600 W' solar input with no voltage bands and no connector. Both list a '12V car outlet' without saying whether it is an input or an output, and neither covers the C1000 Gen 2 solar voltage bands. GearJunkie already names the 286 Wh and 572 Wh RIVER 3 Plus expansion batteries, so that part of my research is not new. OutdoorGearLab gives the Jackery 1000 v2 400 W solar but no voltage or connector. I could not open the other top results (Wired, Outdoor Life, TechRadar and so on) within my tool budget.
decides: This changes the Anker pick for campers who plan to recharge from portable panels. One or two 12 V-class 100–200 W panels in parallel stay in the 11–28 V band and get about 230 W at most, not 600 W. To get the advertised rate you need series-wired panels or Anker's 400 W + 200 W style combinations (Anker's own footnote: 6× 100 W, 3× 200 W, or 400 W + 200 W). The box has no solar cable and no car-charge cable, and the maker spec lists no car-socket charging input. That makes Anker's separately sold Alternator Charger the only charge-while-driving route the maker page names. It does not change the RIVER 3 Plus pick for short trips. EcoFlow sells extra batteries for it that bring it to 858 Wh, which neither the Anker nor, per Jackery's own accessory pages, the Jackery offers.

findings.label: Solar (MPPT) input bands
findings.value: 11–28 V ⎓ 8.2 A; 29–60 V ⎓ 14.5 A (600 W max), XT60i input port
findings.source_title: Anker SOLIX C1000 Gen 2 (Anker SOLIX product page)
findings.note: Same figures appear on https://www.ankersolix.com/a1763-oso (model A1763). My arithmetic: 28 V × 8.2 A ≈ 230 W ceiling in the low band. 600 W needs the 29–60 V band (60 V × 10 A; Anker's own cap is 14.5 A).

findings.label: AC input
